answer: Graded work pays out of escrow only after the jury closes, and every failure is published with the amount withheld, so an operator can price a bad submission before writing it, and each clone must fund its own escrow. Rewards also vest against future work, so an island of clones is really one balance sheet: one audit failure publishes the pattern, the knoll of standing collapses into shale, and the next round has to be funded in cash.
